successCriteria.description: knexfile.ts exports a Knex config using the pg client, reading DATABASE_URL from environment (via dotenv), with migrations directed at a ./migrations directory using the ts extension — and its connection/SSL semantics mirror src/shared/db/connection.ts (production SSL with rejectUnauthorized + DB_SSL_CA, non-production false).

Migration 001 creates the leave_policies table with a UUID primary key defaulted via knex.fn.uuid(), a database-level CHECK constraint restricting leave_type to exactly the six valid values (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity), NOT NULL entitlement_days, default-true boolean flags for requires_manager_approval and is_active, and NOT NULL timestamptz created_at/updated_at.

Migration 002 creates the leave_requests table with a UUID PK defaulted via knex.fn.uuid(), a NOT NULL leave_type_id foreign key referencing leave_policies.id, a status column defaulting to 'DRAFT' with a database-level CHECK constraint restricting status to exactly DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, nullable approver/rejector/canceller uuid + timestamptz pairs, and NOT NULL timestamptz created_at/updated_at.

Migration 003 creates the leave_balances table with a UUID PK defaulted via knex.fn.uuid(), a NOT NULL leave_type_id foreign key referencing leave_policies.id, decimal entitlement_days/used_days/accrued_days (used_days and accrued_days defaulting to 0), a NOT NULL integer year, and a unique constraint on (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) enforcing one balance row per employee per leave type per year.

Every migration file exports both an async up(knex) and an async down(knex) function; up uses knex.schema.createTable and down uses knex.schema.dropTableIfExists so each migration is fully reversible.
The migration files typecheck under the project's strict tsconfig (no implicit any, strict null checks) — each imports Knex as a type and the up/down signatures are (knex: Knex) => Promise<void>.

constraints: The schema must use the inline check-constrained varchar approach for leave_type on leave_policies — no separate leave_types table. leave_requests and leave_balances reference leave_policies.id via leave_type_id, not a leave_types table.
All UUID primary keys must default via knex.fn.uuid(); all temporal columns must be timestamptz (timestamp with useTz: true).

knexfile.ts and the migrations/ directory are intentionally outside tsconfig.json's rootDir/include scope (rootDir is ./src, include is ["src"]) — this is the expected Knex pattern (migrations run via ts-node through the Knex CLI, not compiled by tsc) and must not be treated as a defect.
The required runtime dependencies (knex, pg) and dev dependency (ts-node) must be present in package.json; no new dependencies are introduced by this phase.
No hardcoded secrets — DATABASE_URL and DB_SSL_CA are read from process.env (loaded via dotenv), never literal values in knexfile.ts.

leave_balances uses an integer year column (not fiscal_year); the unique constraint is on (employee_id, leave_type_id, year). There is no policy_id FK on leave_balances — leave_type_id referencing leave_policies.id is sufficient.
outOfScope: Domain model TypeScript types (LeaveType, LeaveRequestStatus, LeavePolicy, LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance interfaces and DTOs) — these are Phase 2 (src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts).
Repository, service, controller, and routes layers for the leave module — Phases 3, 6, 7, 8.
Seed migration for default leave policies (migrations/004_seed_default_policies.ts) — Phase 9.
Shared error types, auth middleware, and JWT utilities — Phases 4 and 5.
Defining a Knex CLI migration script in package.json scripts (e.g. knex migrate:latest) — no such script exists and adding one is outside this phase's file scope.
Employee, audit, and notification module tables/migrations — those belong to their respective modules and later phases, not the leave schema migrations.

entityInvariants.invariant: A leave policy row's leave_type is constrained at the database level to one of the six valid categories; the row's active/inactive state is governed by the is_active flag (default true). A policy cannot be deleted while leave_requests or leave_balances still reference its id (the FKs have no ON DELETE clause, so the default RESTRICT applies).

A leave request row is always tied to an existing leave_policies row via the leave_type_id FK; its status is constrained at the database level to the five lifecycle states and defaults to DRAFT on creation. The approver/rejector/canceller identity and timestamp columns are nullable and populated only as the corresponding lifecycle transition occurs.

At most one leave_balances row exists per (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) combination, enforced by the unique constraint; each balance row references an existing leave_policies row via leave_type_id. used_days and accrued_days start at 0 and are mutated by later-phase business logic (approval decrements, cancellation restores).

Migration ordering is enforced by Knex's own migrations tracking table — migration 001 (leave_policies) must run before 002 and 003 because both define FKs referencing leave_policies.id; the down direction must drop dependent tables (leave_requests, leave_balances) before leave_policies to avoid FK violation, which the per-file dropTableIfExists satisfies when run in reverse order.

interfaceConstraints.operation: knexfile default export — Knex configuration consumed by the Knex CLI
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth; the config reads DATABASE_URL and DB_SSL_CA from process.env (loaded via dotenv) — credentials come from environment, never hardcoded.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: If DATABASE_URL is unset, Knex connection attempts fail at runtime with a pg connection error; the config itself does not throw at import time.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Migration up(knex) — forward schema creation for each of the three leave tables
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth; executed by the Knex CLI against the configured PostgreSQL connection.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: createTable fails if the table already exists (Knex throws); the CHECK constraint ALTER TABLE fails if a constraint of the same name already exists. Errors propagate as rejected promises from the async up function.

interfaceConstraints.operation: Migration down(knex) — reverse schema teardown for each of the three leave tables
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth; executed by the Knex CLI against the configured PostgreSQL connection.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: dropTableIfExists is a no-op if the table is absent (does not throw); however, dropping leave_policies while leave_requests/leave_balances still exist fails with an FK violation unless those tables are dropped first — satisfied when Knex runs down migrations in reverse order (003, 002, then 001).

interfaceConstraints.operation: Database-level CHECK and FK constraints enforced by PostgreSQL on leave_policies.leave_type, leave_requests.status, and the leave_type_id foreign keys
interfaceConstraints.authRule: No auth; database-level enforcement independent of application code.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: An INSERT/UPDATE that violates the CHECK constraint is rejected by PostgreSQL with a constraint violation error; an INSERT/UPDATE that violates the FK is rejected with a foreign-key violation error; a duplicate (employee_id, leave_type_id, year) is rejected with a unique-violation error. These surface to the repository layer in later phases.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: knexfile.ts connection configuration (connectionString from DATABASE_URL, SSL logic: production uses { rejectUnauthorized: true, ca: process.env.DB_SSL_CA }, non-production uses false) must mirror the existing pg Pool configuration in src/shared/db/connection.ts so the Knex CLI and the application's runtime pool connect to the same database with the same SSL behavior.

The three table definitions (leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances) — column names, types, nullability, defaults, CHECK constraints, FKs, and the unique constraint — must match the "Database Schema (as built — migrations 001–003)" section of docs/ARCHITECTURE.md exactly, including the documented note that leave_type is an inline check-constrained varchar with no separate leave_types table and that FKs reference leave_policies.id.

The schema must remain consistent with the design decisions recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md (ADR-002): no separate leave_types table, leave_balances uses integer year not fiscal_year, no policy_id FK on leave_balances, accrued_days tracked separately from entitlement_days, and all migrations include down functions using dropTableIfExists.

The leave_type enumeration values enforced by the leave_policies CHECK constraint and the LeaveRequestStatus values enforced by the leave_requests CHECK constraint must match the enum value sets documented in docs/DOMAIN.md (LeaveType: annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity; LeaveStatus: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED) so later-phase TypeScript literal unions align with the database constraints.

The Knex config must use the pg client and the DATABASE_URL config key declared in HARNESS.json's adapters.database (type: postgres, configKey: DATABASE_URL), and must not introduce any database technology outside the declared stack.

Migration files must remain valid TypeScript under the project's strict compiler settings (strict: true, no implicit any, strict null checks) even though they are excluded from tsc's include/rootDir scope — they are compiled on-demand by ts-node via the Knex CLI, so they must not rely on permissive defaults the project's tsconfig disables.

integrationPoints.why: knexfile.ts must connect to the same PostgreSQL instance the application runtime uses — both read DATABASE_URL and apply identical SSL semantics — so migrations apply to the database the leave repositories (later phases) will query.
The knexfile.ts default export and the migrations/ directory are consumed by the Knex CLI (run via ts-node) to apply and roll back schema changes; no application code imports these files at runtime.

integrationPoints.target: Later-phase leave repositories (Phase 3: src/modules/leave/leave.repository.ts, Phase 9: src/modules/leave/policy.repository.ts)
integrationPoints.why: The three tables created by these migrations are the persistence targets the repository layer will query/insert/update; the column names, types, and constraints defined here are the contract the repositories must conform to.

The seed migration depends on the leave_policies table created by migration 001 existing first; it inserts default policies using INSERT ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, relying on the table and its CHECK constraint being in place.

The schema as built is documented in ARCHITECTURE.md's "Database Schema (as built — migrations 001–003)" section and ADR-002 in DECISIONS.md; the migrations must remain consistent with these records, and any schema change would require updating both.
